comment: Record doing the adventure trail
A bit difficult middle section. Be very careful there. Then it gets easier near top.
Got there at 9:30 on a Friday and had no problems with parking. Moderate hike, excellent views, very well maintained trail. Walking/hiking poles were helpful.
Enjoyable. Need proper footwear for rocks. Great view.
Great to walk in sunny conditions, since the trail is mostly in the shadow of the woods. May be too slippery for the rain/mist. Highly recommend trying “Adventure Trail”.

Beautiful views. Not super well marked, great for exploring. Adventure trail was fun, lots of up and down, initial down was the scariest part and after that not too bad. Parking was full when we left at 1pm, only half full when we pulled in at 10am this holiday Monday.
Moderate hike, easy to navigate and great views. Hiked around 11AM which was pretty nice there’s barely anyone on the trail.
Nice trail with great viewpoints at the end. We followed the red trail!
Watch your footing but a great little hike!
Take the adventure trail
A must do for anyone visiting the island. Absolutely breathtaking views. Stuck to the regular red trail and it was a moderate to easy hike.
amazing views! recommend the adventure trail!!
Amazing views! Can be a bit slippery in wet conditions but worth the hike up!
Pretty easy trek. The Adventure trail needs climbing and rapelling gear to climb up or down, which I didn't have .  Seemed pretty awesome. Need to come back, better equipped.
Nice trail with beautiful sites. Some steep rocks on trail to climb over.
Great trail. The hike is easy to moderate, although there are a lot of uneven terrain and some challenging steep spots.
Lovely trail would 100% do again
Great trail. Rocks to navigate. No bugs.
There are a few vertical climbs that require three points of contact for some hikers but for the most part a semi-challenging hike with the views that pay off at the end.

This is definitely on the higher end of the moderate spectrum…but the views are magnificent. Thankfully it was dry while we were there, it would be very slippery in spots if there had been any amount of precipitation in recent days. 
Lots of parking, we did it on a Sunday morning and it was starting to get pretty busy by the time we were back down.
Some sheer drop offs to make sure you keep young kiddos close by at
Good distance hike, family friendly. Can make longer or shorter. Good hiking shoes recommend.
Wow cliffs so high, falling would be bad. Palms: sweaty. Roots and rock good for walks. Would do again on the island so big the island.
Beautiful trail with ups and downs and some rare flowers!
It’s rocky.  Wear good hiking boots
Stay on the red trail. Still difficult in spots but views well worth it
Fantastic hike! Snow still inside the caves on the Adventure Trail. Did the hike May 11th.

There’s a discernible path; however, there are several small “paths” from previous tourists/hikers getting lost. Signage is consistent but not highly visible. 
No maps along the trail (I think is fine considering it’s a generally short trail even on the longer route)
I would not consider dog friendly if your dog is experiencing cliffs for the first time. Wouldn’t recommend bringing high energy city/apartment dogs if you do not intend to keep it tethered to you the entirety of your hike.
Plenty of parking space, nearby convenience store about 8km away.
I haven’t come across any bee/wasp nests
There’s an unsightly quarry at the first small lookout but after that, the look outs are beautiful. It also makes it easier to spot hawks, eagles, woodpeckers, etc.
Suitable for kids/families who don’t mind risking rolling an ankle or pulling a hammy
Beautiful lookout, no snow on the trail
Nicely maintained and well marked trails with difficulty options. The downside for me is that you can hear highway and/or quarry noise for most of the hike.
Not slippery or frozen at all, reasonably well sigh posted but we did miss one turning so was helpful having the map downloaded!

Amazing trail for a day hike. My dog and I did it in just about an hour, including the time it took us to stop and enjoy the lookout. Very easy to follow, only about 2 spots that were a touch confusing. Only passed 2 others on the whole hike. Dog friendly but make sure your dog is agile for the stairs, they’re very steep.

This is a privately owned trail, which was interesting to know. I wish the weather was a little kinder to us, we had to hike in the rain  but the views are worth it. Stunning! Best views of the fall colors with windmills in the background. Took us almost 3 hours out and back  but that's because we were taking our sweet time.
Awesome trail and nice view.
One of the best trails i’ve ever been!
One of the best trail spots in Ontario!
Fun trail with a small bit of rock scrambling and a ladder section

Slippery roots but lovely views. I wish that all Trails had other levels than easy moderate and hard. Because if this was ranked at one for easy, five for moderate and 10 for hard, I would say this would be  a three.
Amazing hike with fantastic views!
Just beautiful, uphill and downhill. Beginning is easy. At the top you get views from everywhere
sick asf
Beautiful views at top
The adventure trail is totally worth it! We (2 adults, and 11 and 7 year old) did the trail with that side adventure and it took us 2.5 hours. The views are amazing.
Vues magnifiques !

A great trail with a great view. If u r physically able I would definitely recommend taking the adventure trail portion of the hike, which includes cool caves and ladders. The only negative about this trip were the bathrooms as they were overflowing and gross

Really good trail and we went early so it was empty. On our way back down, lots of groups heading up, the earlier the better if you can! A couple tricky spots if you have any mobility concerns, but very flat once you’ve done the initial climb.
Good conditions-the rocks weren’t really slippery. The stairs are very manageable-like a ladder. Great views
Lots of up & down. Hiking poles would be helpful.
Beautiful trail. Adventure part of the trail was fun too!  Lookouts are beautiful.
Lovely trail with beautiful views. Adventure trail was hard but fun
A few steep stairs, rocky path, but gorgeous views make it all worth it!
Great trail- did the red loop on my own. Well marked for the directional challenged. lol even had signs for back to the parking
The view at the top is nice with an exposed cliff face to sit on. Otherwise pretty standard trail and gets very busy. Worth hiking up to the top for a cool photo op, but not a must see hike.
Great trail….wonderful view.
Beautiful trail, awesome conditions and no bugs at this time. Busy but it was spaced out enough

Was pretty busy on parts of the trail, have to wait at times as paths may only allow one person at a time.  Do not rely on the portapotty as they were found to be out if water toilet paper and not very clean.  Trail itself it fun.
Too busy

the sound of the highway is with you. 
View nice but doesn't really look like a cup and saucer
Not as impressive as the Himalayas but the views were worth the hike. It
Fantastic views and lockouts. Follow the red trail easier it took us 5.6km and 2.5 hours. We stop to eat, took pics and so on.
I hiked around 5pm in late August and the trail was empty! Completed in 1h15m at a brisk walking pace
Had to turn around. I had two dogs one of them a German Shepherd. Stairs are too steep and too wet without handrails.
Amazing trail. Did the adventure trail with 4&6 year olds and it was amazing.
Beautiful trail

Great trail and views 

Sad that we didn’t see the property dogs on the trail though lol
A lot of really nice lookouts. Was there on a frieday afternoon. At this time there were a lot of people on the trail...
We, two fit 66-year-olds found the Adventure Trail to be fairly adventurous. The cave was too narrow to go through for us.
Excellent trail for myself and 9 year old son ! Wear good running shoes.  Hiking shoes / boots are ideal for adventure trail

Got here around 10:30 was wasn’t too bad parking readily available wasn’t too many people out on the trail. Got back 1230 and it’s packed so definitely earlier is better. Great trail amazing views well worth it to go around if you wanna do the adventure Trail you need to pay attention to the first entrance as I missed it and found the exit. Otherwise get to the top.

The trail is really nice but it is really busy and hard to get parking. The stair are more like ladders making it not very good for dogs the view at the top is beautiful and totally worth the hike. Parts of the trail is climbing over big rocks. If you are looking for more adventure. I would recommend the slide trail called adventure trail it is more challenging and if you pay attention along the trail there are caves and different rocks to climb. Some of the caves are really tiny so I wouldn’t recommend doing it if you are worried you won’t fit. All of the caves start on the side trail and end on the side trail so you don’t have to worry about getting lost. I would totally recommend the trail and if you’re able to I would also recommend the adventure trails it makes the hike more fun.
Great view.  Go early.  Crowded by 10.
Lots of rocky features and a lot of uphill. Amazing views from the tops! Cool stairs. Longer options and adventure options. Regular trail is great and lots of fun!
Great view at top

One of my favourite trails in the province. It is one of the best views for the easiest effort kind of trails, and aside from a couple of small ascent sections it's mostly flat and shaded by canopy. The adventure trail provides some additional challenges if you seek it (and I recommend it if you're an avid hiker) but this trail is lovely throughout. It's difficult to find parking some summer weekends so keep that in mind.

Pretty flat with the exception of a few rock scrambles, one ladder/staircase, and an awkward section where you have to squeeze beside a boulder. Signage is confusing and I would've taken some wrong turns if not for having a map on AllTrails. Views are decent.
Not worth the visit, views were ok ok, no mountains. Just trees and that too covered with smoke. Adventure trails was fun. I would go visit some other place than this trail
Great trail, it gets pretty busy by noon,
Rocky and slippery

Was a great hike after a 5 hour car ride to get to Manitoulin island, started at 3:30 and trail is very shaded so not too hot, took us about an hour and 50 minutes stopping to take a few minutes taking it in ad pics of course! We enjoyed it!

Wouldn’t recommend for small city dogs or clumsy dogs. 
Lots of squirrels and small birds. Dogs w prey drive should be in a choke chain or a heavy duty leash/collar
Some parts are a little rocky n steep
The adventure trail is fun. I’d like it if it was longer
Great views, steep climbs and if you can, do the “adventure trail” near the loop.
Great Trail. Stunning views at the top. Please be careful with pets and children however as the cliffs are very dangerous. Aside from the it's a must try.
The railing on the first ladder could use some repair- otherwise a great trail
Beautiful trail! Great scenery, and great conditions.
It’s little slippery after rain, wear proper hiking shoes.. the trail is really good and challenging.. the view from the lookout point is amazing
Amazing views as always. Well take care of trail!

It's a very easy trail. We hiked in the rain so some of the rocks were a bit slippery. There are some short stairs. Nothing too dangerous. Watch out for billions of mosquitoes. They were super annoying. Bug spray is a must. Otherwise, it's a very basic trail. Nothing too spectacular or interesting to see, other than the lookout. I think this hike is a bit overrated.

Very nice trail, hot day, pretty views, a quarry is visible from some of the first few lookouts. Unfortunately we were convinced to turn back by other hikers on the trail and missed the last few lookouts. Maybe we’ll get to see them all next time  Happy 26th Birthday to Eric and I hope he enjoys his bday surprise
Beautiful views, many rocky bits, wear good shoes.

Well marked and maintained trail. AllTrails navigation is spot on and helpful in areas with denser vegetation. Amazing views and multiple viewpoints throughout! Adventure trail requires good shoes as there's some minor climbing involved.

Easy / Moderate difficulty, some climbing, nice views. It was raining for the first half so muddy but not overly.
Few if any bugs present.

Adventure trail worth the hike, would rate as Easy / Moderate 
Some of the climbs make it more moderate with the ladder and rock climbs
Hard to park on long weekends but worth it! Gorgeous trail views!

Did the shorter (red) loop along with the adventure trail. Went clockwise with the adventure loop first, and felt this was better. There was a lot of noise for the first half as there was a mine (?) operating near by, but the latter half facing away from the mine was quiet and had even better views. Not busy, bugs not bad
Lotsa rocks and roots, but great views at the cliff

Trail was well marked
Clean well, maintain trail
Beautiful trail, did counter clockwise starting with the woods and saved the lookouts for later.
Awesome views + dog friendly !!
rams head and lady slipper orchids if you come during the right season!
Very beautiful but a bit difficult trail. We enjoyed it a lot!!
Beautiful hike!! Amazing view at the top!
Followed the red trail but got lost at one point so turned back unfortunately.  Pay attention to tree markings because there are paths that aren’t the trail.
It’s a nice trail. There are several lookout points… nice views, photos cannot do enough justice for its beauty…
The view is well worth the hike. Watch out for poison ivy at the overlook
Unreal views

You’re in for a treat with these look outs. The landscape is truly unique and the trail for the most part is very well marked. We also took the offshoot to the adventure trail. I’d say the entire trail is easy-moderate and that the adventure trail is difficult-moderate. It had rained for 3 days straight prior to today so the adventure trail had a few slippery rocks. Super cool getting to climb the ladder and go through the caves. Overall, I highly recommend!

The view from the highest point (east bluff) is amazing !
Go during morning hours around 8-9am to beat the crowd and also get parking easily, becomes crowded later in the day.

Dog friendly but have to be leashed specially at the highest point where it is steep
Absolutely wicked views, especially on the east side. If you have decent shoes, take the adventure trail for some fun!
No snow or ice on trial on May 1st. Good views for an easy hike. There is a short but quite steep set of stairs with a rail.
I did this trail in April and some parts of trail still had snow, which turned to ice and made it slippery. This made the hike moderately difficult. But otherwise its an easy hike.

Looks like there’s rare winter use. Parking is not plowed, “no stopping” signs along the highway. We had our work cut out for us breaking trail in snow shoes but it’s possible. We had to be careful with some deep crevices under the snow.
My all time favourite Fall hike! I'll never get tired of this view

The trail was an overall beautiful hike. We went in mid October and the colours were incredible! I would say if you are older, have joint issues or balance issues to maybe skip this trail, there are lots of rocks on the trail and uneven ground and can be pretty hard on the feet. We did the red trail

Beautiful views off the cliffs. The quarry at a couple lookout points is kind of an eyesore but once you get to the bigger lookouts, it’s gone! Definitely recommend wearing proper footwear, the terrain is rough! There are stairs and a few tough climbing areas but overall an amazing trail.

Wear good hiking shoes. Don’t pull rocks out of the limestone walls. This trail is marked excellent and was very clean. Had a great day. Take your lunch to eat at the escarpment for the views are beautiful.
Be careful with the cliffs at the tops
My husband and I hiked the trail  today! Moderate trail u have to watch out for roots and rocks! Beautiful views of manitoulin island!
Amazing trail, short and easy to do, amazing views

Nice hike up to the viewing cliffs on a Sunday in Sept.  A lot of people.  Young guys smoking weed at the top .  One guy was sitting up in a tree!   Large gravel parking area, 2 porta potties.  The trail is quite rocky and there is one set of very steep stairs with a wobbly railing.   I'm going to guess that this is not a good trail for people with bad knees or hips.
Nice and easy trail. Not crowded. Pet friendly.
Beautiful and interesting trail, well shaded with stunning views at the top. Excellent trail conditions. Will have to come back to try out the full loop next time!
The Adventure trail is really cool. Bring a flashlight or have a cell phone with a flashlight. Plenty of places to park and big signs to alert you where to park. Trail is well marked too.
Nice hike. Did it with my 3 year old on my back. My 5 year old did the whole hike herself. It an get slippery in the rain so sturdy shoes are a must!
Count for a comfortable  2 hrs round trip for the hike

Stunning views at the end of this trail. We went on a gloomy day and there was a fair amount of people so I assume it gets pretty busy with better weather. This hike has some steep parts and was sometimes difficult to know where to go. However I would highly recommend going!
Nice trail- we took the adventure portion of the trail which was great! It’s well shaded but bring a bit of water. It took us just under 2 hours in total with stops.
Very nice challenging hike. Tons of people go here so depending on the time of year you may have a hard time finding parking.
It’s 5.5 km.  Beautiful lookouts
Arrive early to avoid crowds and have room to park. Dry conditions today.
Great!  A little crowded.  But beautiful as ever.
Such a lovely fun trail with beautiful sweeping views at the end. Mostly shaded. Massive free parking lot.
Fairly easy. Great views.
Fun trails and a moderate hike. Wear proper footwear. No flip flops.
Easy trail with great views. Do the adventure trail for a bit more fun! Got to see some caves, cool rock formations, climb ladders, etc... at the top there is great views of the island!!
Walked in for sunrise on the east bluff and it was worth the early morning alarm

Amazing trail for the views and obstacle aspect to keep it interesting. Trail was short and easy, and almost disappointing in a way as it was too easy to get such a spectacular view. Plus an easy trail means WAY more people. But luckily there is a MULTITUDE of cliff access points to get some killer pictures and views. Don't be that person that turns around after the first viewpoint! Walk a little further past the loop end section and you won't regret it. If time was permitting I would have done the whole loop but I spent WAY too long up top admiring the view so ended up turning back. But the trail seems to follow along the cliff and so you get constant viewpoints. Or just hike that section first and not go left like I and many others did. I kind of wish I did do that and not follow the reviews of others. DON'T FORGET the adventure trail section, and when you come to a crevice that makes you wonder 'what's down there?' GO DOWN THERE. It's a super short tunnel that leads out past the rocks with a ladder. I actually missed this on the way up and saw the ladder on the way back and realised what it was.
Take the adventure trail!!
Lots of rocks and over grown tree roots makes it difficult is spots

The weather was great, around 20c and sunny for a change, AND NO BUGS.

I’ll rate this as moderate difficulty as there are some steep inclines and declines, gaps in rocks, crevasses, and various protruding roots, typical of Niagara Escarpment trails.  The trails are also well marked and worn.  

A little more difficult if one chooses to take the Adventure Trail, as it’s a bit technical – climbing ladders and squeezing through tight spaces in the crevasses.  Caution needs to be exercised if you are bringing kids or pets as there are a lot of cliffs, VERY steep cliffs, about 90M (295Ft), however the views from up there are AMAZING!  Another satisfying and well needed escape in nature.

Ensure you have PROPER clothing while taking this or any trail; footwear with good traction and ankle support, proper outdoor clothing, water, and other outdoors "essentials" will make your hike a safe and enjoyable one.
Great trail! Easy-moderate with amazing views! Very busy despite being a Monday afternoon and the parking lot was pretty full.
Amazing views, take the adventure trail for extra fun of climbing on rocks and ladder!
A beautiful trail that offers three routes - one for the extremely adventurous. The terrain is rocky and full of roots which i loved. A must visit for its breathtaking views.

We completed this hike with a group with an age range of 6-65. The main trail was moderate - do able for most people who do not have mobility concerns. Some parts were very rocky/rooty, so grippy running shoes or hiking shoes are recommended. It hasn’t rained for a bit here, so the trail was not muddy. However, I imaging it would get fairly muddy/slippery after a rain. Part of our group took the “Adventure” side trail. They enjoyed going through the crevices - that section of the trail was quite challenging for some of the group.
Wonder to ocky lots of roots great views to
Between easy and moderate. There is a couple of challenging climbs at the ladder and some rock trails.
Wear good hiking shoes and bring water. This is a serious hike. Absolutely breath-taking views. Well worth the work.
This trail is not suitable for dogs. Very steep stairs, rugged terrain and abrupt cliffs.
Tons of people no horses
Beautiful views and rocky trails:) recommended!

We started the trail at 6am, got to the top around 7am. Had the whole trail to ourselves. Didnt see anyone else until 2/3s of the way back down. If you go early it’s awesome. There are some short steep/ rocky chunks, including an incredibly steep stairway/ladder thing. Dogs may have difficulty.
The trail has some rocky parts and slanted paths, so make sure to wear shoes with good grip.
Took over 3 hours with our 3.5 year old.  Had to carry him for parts of the trail.  Beautiful views and a challenging but fun hike.
Rather rocky and some places do involve climbing, so not appropriate for people with mobility issues or looking for an easy hike. I’d caution bringing dogs.
Beautiful walk. Go earto avoid the heat and crowds
Bring your camera great look outs
many lookouts. slippery rocks when wet. can get busy. lots of parking. come on a cool day. solid inclines on the way up
absolutely amazing
Adventure trail is nice but not super easy. Overall nice trail but gets quite busy midday

Bring water, sturdy shoes, first aid kit, hat, sunscreen, hiking pole helps too! Don’t forget your phone/camera and your energy you will need it! Awesome views and gorgeous hike! Great for photography enthusiasts!
Nice hike. Views are great.  Good for anyone that doesn’t need flat and level.
The trail  was AMAZING!! Not crowded, great cardio and amazing views
Beautiful day for a hike with the pup
Best view! Take adventure trail along the main path to see the caves and neat ladders. Took me 2 hours to complete with a big group including two kids.
Perfect day- mid July. Two muddy spots but there were rocks to walk upon to get you through.
a bit tricky with baby carrier, 1 crevice and steep carrier. otherwise great trek with great views
Great views.  Slippery rocks

we went on a Sunday before 9 am and not many people.  By noon it was getting busy. 
 Definitely 
bring good hiking shoes and
 trekking poles if you have them.  Great trail.

For July 2, trail was remarkably bug  free with cool breezes.   Not a difficult hike, between easy and moderate. Enjoyed the limestone pavements and views.  Did not enjoy two hundred plus people and many dogs on the trail.  The trail is easy to follow and very well worn. 

















 and many dogs on the trail.  The trail is showing
The uphills are challenging.
must visit while in the Manitoulin area!
Adventure loop was great.  The trail well maintained and easy to follow.
Nice little hike. Well marked, nice views
Great hike and views! Beware of the final step of the stairs on the way down. Very loose and could result in injury.
Did the red trail and it was challenging enough with lots of rocks and elevation. Really well marked. Great views but not suitable for small children
Overall in good condition, beautiful viewpoints. Beware some noise from quarry nearby.
I took the red trail and it was well marked throughout. I also took my time and spotted an owl and some other interesting birds. Great views from the overlook

Beautiful trail. Please wear appropriate hiking shoes. Many stunning views. Pleasantly surprised to see very little trash. I recommend continuing on the hike with the blue  trail( wear pants). It’s lovely and well marked & very solitary.

Trail Condition on May 26th: Well marked (red route) and maintained trail.  Some sections of the trail are slippery due to the rainfall. Make sure you have proper footwear. Plenty of shade throughout the hike. 

Parking: Plenty of parking available when we visited. There is also an overflow parking area. The main route takes avg time of  1hr 45min so you will find some parking spots clear up even on busy days. 

The viewpoint is amazing. Please make sure your dogs are restrained and kids supervised.  Very sheer cliffs.
Stairs and rocks were slippery.  Used trekking poles for the first time, I’ll never go hiking without them.  Need good hiking boots. Great view at the top.
Good quick hike. Easier end of the range. Lots of potential detours and alternative paths (i.e “Adventure Trail”). Recommend and all size dog friendly.

The cup and saucer .
t
Trail gets tight around times, but it's a hood challenge.

An easy trail, well marked with a couple of spots where we had to climb ladders. Did the 4K route. Started at 7 in the morning to beat the heat and the bugs. Lovely views from the top. 
No muds and the parking space was spot on.
There's a grove before heading up the mountain to the lookout that is magical.  Great hike.  Had the place to myself first thing in the morning this time of year.
Definitely need good shoes or hiking shoes. Look outs don’t have any safety railings

Lovely little trail. So much change in the scenery to keep it interesting, my favourite kind of hike. 
Took us almost 2 hours with our dog

I would caution two things: 1. Very mucky at the beginning of the trail, wear boots!
2.there are some parts of the red trail that still get pretty steep and rocky so proceed with caution if you aren’t confident with heights or making steep descents

Otherwise, if you are able-bodied and enjoy some challenge this is a proper hike with beautiful views and the trail along the way has so many cool rocks, trees, and animals! We absolutely loved it. Well marked and easy to find as well as navigate.
Little bit muddy at the trailhead but once you gain elevation it is fine. Had trail to myself, 10/10
amazing trail!
Beauty cliff views, a few sheer cliffs and holes in the path to be careful of but all around not particularly difficult trek long as your prepared!

Only one other vehicle there today. We hiked the red trail to the lookouts and then took the adventure trail before heading back to the car. Still some ice and snow sections so take caution. Completed the trail with a 5 year old with zero issues.

Wonderful time of the year to hike this trail! 24°C and NO BUGS! Some steep sections, but once at the top it's moderately level! And then it's all downhill on the way back! Wear good hiking boots as the terrain can be quite rough. If you're even slightly adventurous, take the adventure trail (yellow) and follow the glimpses of blue into crevices and caves. At one point it will seem like you have lost the trail, stay close to the escarpment and you will find the ladders!
Gorgeous fall colour
Great for dogs. Well groomed with moderate challenges. The views are absolutely stunning and a must see.

More challenging than I was expecting, one of the rockiest hikes I've done. Once you get to the stairs it ramps up from pretty easy to leg burner. 
Would not suggest bringing any littles.

When we arrived there were 2 small parking lots and some porta potties. We decided to hike the shorter trail of the 2. The climb was moderate and wasn't too difficult. I would say just have some good footwear on. We went first thing in the morning so we ended up having the place to ourselves up at the top. It was  an amazing view and absolutely worth the hike.
Be prepared for challenging scrambling over steep rocky sections. Trail starts out deceptively level through mostly cedar woods.
The adventure trail was full of surprises. Be on the lookout for the cave passages!
Rocky with some steep parts
Calorie burner for sure
A fun trail with some interesting climbing and scrabbles over rocks and roots, leading to stunning views.
Very enjoyable trail. A bit difficult - one steep staircase about 15 steps and some high steps. Takes about an hour to get to the top.

Gets busy after around 10am 
Trails are good condition and moderately easy but there is some elevated climbing
Well marked, adventurous, tight on parking. Love the caves and impromptu rock scrambling!
Vistas are beautiful....trail is easy. It's just busy. So many families, kids, dogs. Too busy for my liking but worth the views.
Exiting trail
Great views, alternative ability options, beautiful and clean trail, with great and helpful signage.

There are two main loops, one 5 km and one 11 km plus a few "adventure trails" which are more challenging shortcuts.  The 5 km has a few moderate climbs but you are rewarded with 4 spectacular outlooks from the top of the escarpment.  You'll see quite a few other hikers. If you chose to continue and complete the 11 km instead of looping back, you'll get one or two additional views and see very few people for the rest of the way. The trail is well packed but has rocks and roots sticking up. We saw young children and seniors making the 5 km. There are ntwo parking lots but they fill up in high season. There are also a couple of portable toilets. The only negative on this hike was a noisy quarry at the bottom of the escarpment about half way through.

Ended up just doing the red and yellow route because we spent lots of time just enjoying the amazing views of Lake Manitou and the island. Do the adventure trail section if you can. Easy crawl throughs and short climbs. Our kids 4 & 8 loved the challenge.
Take adventure trail ! It's real fun
busy but amazing
Great trail! Not much of a hike but super pretty lookouts. The “adventure trail” is where you find the caves and the ladders to climb up

Great hike. 5.29km on my watch from the parking lot and back. The adventure trail was worth it with the kids, 5 and 7 years old. A few spots had steep ladders, so difficult for dogs. Fun caves to go thru. I would take it up versus down, next time. Less scary for parents! lol
No bugs, nice shade on a hot day. beautiful view.
A couple steep spots, but nothing too hard. Great views at the top.
Trails were well marked and views were spectacular.
Amazing view at the top, need to be careful while ascending with some of the rocky terrain.
Stairs and rocky climbs, the mostly flat. Lots of shade
Great trail but be careful of the Poison Ivy on the trail. Great views!

Great viewpoints on a fun hike. Only a few bugs, despite being after a rain. Very kid friendly (as long as they know to stay away from sheer cliffs).

Would have tried the adventure trail, but it was still slippery and muddy after the rain.
Great views, steep in places.  Slippery when wet, use hiking footwear.

Very fun and adventurous! There’s no spots where it’s a constant uphill so you don’t get winded and quickly. There’s options for less rocky paths, but if you’re feeling adventurous there’s lots of fun alternative routes! Just like the other comments said, make sure to come early if you want to hike in the peace and quiet.

S-tier ontario trail. Views to effort ratio are off the scale here, and the adventure trail is tons of fun. Parking lot fills fast in the summer. Trail conditions are amazing right now, and oddly there were no bugs at all when I went earlier in the day. Amazin
No bugs, wear good shoes and be careful. Rocks can be slippery
Beautiful trail! No bugs at all this time of year, busy and loud, some construction noise
Nice!
Perfect conditions. Lot of social media influncers on the trail! Haha.
Trail was dry, no bugs and not too hot. Great day to hike. Always a little busy this time of year tho

Trail conditions were very dusty when dry/hot. Rocks are slippery even when dry from travel, worse when wet. Some steep sections but generally an easy hike even for non avid hikers. 

Can be busy in three summer months.

Combined distance of all trails (includes the Adventure Trail and the Blue Trail): 10.57km
Moving time: 2h 40 min
Stopped time: 1h 38 min
Things to Bring: Water, Binoculars, Lunch, Blanket (or lightweight portable chairs)

The trail is most famous for the breathtaking views from the top of the escarpment - and they are spectacular. We’ve taken in the views in both June and late-September, and both times of year have their special charms. In June the forest is lush and cooling, and wildflowers are evident along the trails. In late-September the forest is ablaze with fall colours which are particularly beautiful when viewed from on high. 

Another aspect of the trail gets less comment but is worthy of mention. The walk provides you with a chance to get up close and personal with the magnificent geological formations of the Niagara escarpment. Stand next to huge chunks of solid stone with deep slices carved by thousands of years of rain. Marvel at how trees sink their roots in between layers of rock, becoming one with the stone, stubbornly thriving.

Red Trail:
The is the trail that leads from the parking lot to the famous views at the top of the escarpment. It’s a fairly easy walk, but it does require decent mobility as some portions have short but steep vertical sections that require you to clamour over a few large rocks. It takes you to the top of the bluffs and then along the cliff side offering a number of spectacular views of sweeping forests, distant lakes, and the bluffs themselves.  We got a close up look at a Downy Woodpecker and a family of Grouse, as well as a number of butterfly species. Tiger Lilies were plentiful along the trailside during our mid-June visit. 

The first part of the trail is a gradual ascent but a couple of spots require navigating some large rock formations and climbing a short but steep ladder. The ground also has some narrow deep crevasses in spots where water has worn through the rock, so keep young children and dogs close.  The viewpoints are along steep cliff faces - mind your footing and don’t get unnecessary close to the edge. 

Adventure Trail:
The “Adventure Trail”, marked in yellow, is a 500 metre trail adjacent to the Red Trail. It’s a lot of fun with some challenging footwork and fascinating rock formations. You’ll find a ladder that takes you into a cave and one that takes you up onto a rocky, secluded perch. This trail should be avoided in wet conditions - it just cries out for a sprained ankle or broken wrist.  

Blue Trail: 
We chose to walk this loop to come down from the Red Trail lookout points. We like to take this trail because it is much less travelled and provides less busy viewpoints along the top section. The blue trail is a bit rocky and uneven in parts, but generally it’s long stretches of very pleasant nature path through shaded trees; this is a great trail for hot summer days.

The Blue Trail is clearly marked overall, but there are two points that can be a bit confusing. You’ll run into a maintenance road (45.8420398, -82.1117584) - this is not part of the trail.  Look across the maintenance road along the tree line and you’ll see blue markers (some blue trail tape as well) that mark where you are meant to re-enter the trees and connect to the ongoing trail. Past this point further down the trail seems to split as well -  to our left we noticed a well-travelled foot path that had a rope hanging across it. Take note: that was not the way to go. We went right and eventually rejoined the Red Trail that took us back to the parking lot.

Hidden View Point:

Just off the Blue Trail. This viewpoint has a large area of flat rock and is less visited than the other spots.  Great place to bring portable chairs or a picnic blanket, and hill a while.

There are also the cleanest, non-smelly porta-potties I've ever used with tissues and sanitizers at the parking lot. I gave 4 stars due to how crowded it was.
Beautiful!!
Amazing views well worth any hike
Great trail!  Some challenging parts for 5 year olds. Lots of dogs but most were on leashes so it wasn’t an issue. Beautiful lookout and well worth it.
It’s a good trail! Beautiful cliffs and great view from up above!
Amazing trail, moderate difficulty with a lot of rocks and change in elevation.  Breathtaking views.
Amazing trail beautiful look out and view.

What a  hoot I had!   I thought the trails were very pretty and easy to navigate and the view?  So worth it!  I would highly recommend taking the 'Adventure' loop it's not terribly long before the lookout (ends very close to lookout).  It's as it states, an adventure, and I loved it.  So many beautiful rocks carved into the mountain to see but can be a bit tricky to navigate, I say go for it!!  :)
Moderate trail with some tough spots for small kids or those who require some additional support. Worth it for the amazing views!
It was a very nice hicking! Kids friendly!

Such a fun hike, about 30 mins there and back, some areas are straight forward others are a little rocky and there is a set of stairs that’s are tiny but steep to go up so wear good hiking shoes or running shoes. Such amazing views though and worth it!
Short trail and straight forward. Only did the lookouts (skipped the blue trail and the whole loop). Stunning views at the lookout (unfortunately all I saw were more trees and lakes in the distance)
short and sweet..
Great trail!! Highly recommend! Great views!! Don’t miss this one!!
Well traveled and marked trail. Fairly easy with only a few challenging sections. Great expansive views
Amazing view! Worth The trip to go to this hiking trail!
very good trail. the yellow adventure trail is poorly marked. enjoy the good view at the end. easy walk with kids

Fun fun fun! Adventure trail super fun (though we did get lost a little... luckily the app brought us back!!). The view is incredible. Ever wanted to feel like you’re on Pride Rock? This is the place. A must see truly.
Very nice, family friendly trail with beautiful view

I would honestly recommend this trail to anyone. The scenery is absolutely breathtaking. I went on this hike alone. I only came across one couple that was with their 3 dogs. I did the adventure trail and am so happy I had this app because I veered off trail a couple of time and used the map with the waypoints I added to find my way back. The adventure trail was amazing, definitely more on the moderate side. I recommend some good hiking shoes as the trail is rocky at some areas. Bring some bug repellent. If you do decide to hike this trail during the summer, plan ahead and go early in the day before it gets too hot, there is some good shading from the trees in some areas. Overall it was very clean and the markers were clear. Can’t wait to go back in the fall!
Lots of snow, so difficult to hike
amazing view
Very good condition. We visited after a rain and it made the trail difficulty increase. Beautiful views and changing topography.

Fun hike to do with the kids. Well marked trail with option for an “adventure” trail. Kids loved that side trail.  Trail has changed in the last few years so if you haven’t done it in the past five or so years the entrance has changed. Very popular trail go early for fewer people
Amazing lookouts very popular trail!

The trail is not like it used to be, it has completely changed. The view is absolutely beautiful and the trail it self is nice. There is not much climbing and if you park on the road your car will be towed.

Great trail, the views up top and phenomenal! The trail is well worn, however many of the marking for the trail had seemingly been ripped off the tree from passers by. 

The trail has a few climbs, some pretty steep but over all isn’t pretty modest. One section does have wooden stairs. The hike would be pretty easily done by kids or elder adults with reasonable fitness. 

The cliffs from the top are very steep and a fall would certainly be fatal, so be careful when near the face, especially with pets and children.

Really good trail especially if you do the adventure trail part as well. The adventure trail can get tricky and, I would say, not for beginners. The lookout is worth the hike. Proper hiking shoes are a must as the trail is rocky.
very scenic and well signed
A nice moderate hike on well-maintained trails. The view from the lookout is amazing.

really easy hike and very enjoyable.

trail was very well marked and straight forward.

did the red loop in 1.5 hours with stops to take photos at all the view points.
Wonderful hike with diverse trails and awesome views!
Great views with a few steep parts

Beautiful trail , bit rocky in parts. Its not a hard trail but neither can be classified as easy. However anybody with moderate level of activity can complete this trail. Saw many kids and dogs in the trail too.
Great trail. Amazing view from the top. Worth every step.
Busy trail, amazing lookouts. I would consider it easy as the terrain is pretty even and so is the path.
worth every step

Moderate trail. Wish we would have had the time to do the extra 5k. Recommend doing the whole 6 mile loop if you can. Take all the pics. Great views and a good adrenaline rush, especially if you don't do heights ;) 
Don't pass on this one.
Great trail. It’s a cool wet Monday so nobody else out. Quiet
I went there in summer, there are 3 mini trails blue, red and green. Beautiful place with an amazing view. I saw a snake and chipmunks and squirrels. Great place

As some one from the area originally I’ve climbed this trail dozens of times and it is quite fun. Plenty of different terrains for everyone with wonderful views of the island. Watch out for Massasauga Snakes as they are venomous and common in the area. Not the most clearly marked trail and definitely not the most leisurely hike either.
completed the Red Trail, there was some difficulty/ rock to climb but lots of breaks between. went one Lookout Into the Blue Trail which I believe is the best Lookout

So there is three parts to this trail the blue trail, the red trail, and the yellow trail. All parts make the trail 9.5 km. You start on the red trail which is 4km and includes all the lookouts, from there you can either go back or continue into the blue trail which is 5km and has no lookouts but is an easier hike in a lovely deciduous forest. There is a small trail that goes off of red trail called the adventure trail which what my favourite part. Has ladders and caves to climb into. But be warned, if you bring your dog, the adventure trail has a ladder you will have to carry it up (thank god mine is only 20 lbs). 
The red trail is extremely busy, even on a Wednesday! But only saw two other couples on the blue trail. Blue trail is much less marked but is obvious where to go. Took us 3 hours to do all 9.5km.
Nice trail! They changed it a little bit and the trail now starts from the highway approximately 2km to the west of the original one.

Nice trail with some variation. Much of it is through the forest on a well worn path. Some ascent required along the escarpment. Great views from the edge of the escarpment. Lots of options for shortening or lengthening the route by either taking the inland forest path and/or adventure trail.
Great trail with gorgeous views as a reward at the end. Did the hike with my Australian Shepherd, so it is a very dog friendly hike.
great trail, did it during spring break, still tons of snow.. would definitely not suggest going in the winter. hard to climb
Awesome trail, great views!
Very well marked with an outstanding view! ♡
Wow, what a fun and challenging hike! The views off the bluffs are spectacular and the adventure trail added to the excitement. New trailhead was easy to find. Highly recommended!!!
Awesome viewing point, I would recommend for sure.
love this trail great views great family hike especially if you have little monkeys in the family
Amazing segment of the Niagara Escarpment!

Our family of five did this trail as our first difficult hike.  We did it backwards and ended up on the adventure trail last.  It turned into our reward for finishing and taking 4 hours for little kids (8,11 & 14) . Beautiful lookouts.  Bring snacks and water!
I did this trail all the time when I still lived at home. Loved the scenery lots of wildlife.

There are a number  great lookout points along the trail to enjoy. Most of the trail is easy with some sections of moderate difficulty. The adventure trails are well worth exploring.  Unfortunately , the trail is not marked very well in various spots. The one negative is the presence of an aggregates business that comes right up against the trail early on. Other than that, it is a hike well worth taking.

Disappointing.  The active quarry on the edge of the trail was disturbingly  distracting.  The loud heavy machinery and the smell of diesel fuel was a stark contrast to the sights and it took too long hiking at a good pace to get away from it.
Awesome little jaunt in the woods.
